page: Amazon Web Services c7a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9R14 processor. This x86_64 architecture server features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1994.0 and a bzip3 single-threaded decompression rate of 13.79 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. Text processing performance is particularly notable, achieving a top-tier Geekbench text processing score of 2762.0, which ranks in the top 10%. Multi-core performance is moderate, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 10286.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 18308.68, both aligning with average tier expectations.

A primary hardware tradeoff is the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, which restricts memory-intensive operations. This limitation is reflected in the uncached large-block memory read bandwidth of 38.63 GB/sec, which falls into the bottom 25% of benchmarks. Additionally, while the instance handles small-model LLM text generation efficiently at 280.04 tokens/sec, performance drops to a weak 7.9 tokens/sec for medium 7B models. Qualitatively, the instance offers high compute density per resource unit for CPU-bound tasks that do not require massive memory footprints or local storage.

Given these characteristics, the c7a.2xlarge is suited for compute-heavy workloads such as text processing, single-threaded data decompression, batch processing, and lightweight machine learning inference on small models. It is also appropriate for static web serving and general-purpose compute tasks that fit within its 16.0 GB memory limit.
